title.narrative: FTF Bangladesh Aquaculture and Nutrition Activity

description.narrative: (Bangladesh): .The Bangladesh Aquaculture and Nutrition activity coordinates linkages among value chain actors across private, public, and civil society spheres. By providing FY 2021 funding to develop the capacity of hatchery owners, nursery owners, fish fingerling sellers, fish feed manufacturers, feed dealers, and a broad range of supporting services, firms will continue to grow and contribute to building the capacity of all aquaculture value chain players, including women, within the southern regions of Bangladesh. The activity's technical assistance will improve productivity, production, and quality of aquaculture systems and strengthen market systems with expanding opportunities for women and youth. Through targeted messaging and technical service on diversification of household production, smallholder aquaculture households will gain greater awareness to adopt nutrition-enhancing behaviors. Value chain actors will also receive training on improved production practices and technologies and sub-grants for piloting innovations and the scale-up of successful ones. To reduce the COVID-19 impact, the activity will strengthen local markets for sales and supply of aquaculture produce, support mechanization to reduce labor costs and the effects of labor shortages and increase the financial resilience of small and medium enterprises and their ability to mitigate and recover from the shock...This activity will support the Global Food Security Strategy and significantly contribute to achieving the State-USAID Joint Strategic Plan Goal Two, and the U.S. government's mission objective of improved food security in Bangladesh. Funding within this IM contributes to meeting the required Host Community ($600K), Adaptation (Indirect), and Micro, Small and Medium Sized Enterprises directives..
